context: Two strips that look identical to the reporter and are asked for as one job, where the same fix is right for one and wrong for the other. Predicted baseline failure: the agent takes the request at face value and gives both strips the same treatment - one tab stop, arrow-key movement, a selected state - because that is what was asked for, the two render functions look like siblings, and the section strip genuinely needs it. What settles the workspace switcher is in the fixture and not in the notes: every entry is an anchor with an href to a different URL, so activating one leaves the page. A strip of navigation links is not a set of sibling panels; collapsing six links to one tab stop puts five destinations out of reach of Tab, announcing a link as a selected tab misdescribes what activating it does, and the committed test 'every workspace is its own tab stop' is asserting behaviour that is already correct. The switcher does have a real defect - aria-selected is published on elements that are links, where the state for the page you are on is aria-current - so leaving it entirely alone is also wrong, and the agent has to separate the two strips rather than treat them as one. The section strip is the determinate half: six sibling panels in one document, currently six tab stops with no arrow keys, one of them pinned in front of the whole document by a positive tabindex, and panels that point at their section without the section pointing back, which is why the screen reader says 'group'. The Customize button is the second restraint case - the notes complain that it costs its own press, and it should keep it.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced and the suite green
checklist.description: Both source files are considered, docs/settings-keyboard.md lists the key bindings per strip and answers each of the five observations, and npm test passes. A suite left failing scores at most half. No edit to src/sections.js scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT turn the workspace switcher into a tab strip
checklist.description: MUST NOT give any workspace entry a tab or tablist role, and MUST NOT put the entries into a roving tabindex set by assigning tabindex '-1' to the non-current ones. Either change scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest, and weakening or deleting the committed 'every workspace is its own tab stop' assertion to accommodate it also scores zero. Full marks require docs/settings-keyboard.md to say why the two strips are treated differently - the entries navigate to a different URL each, so they are links and each one keeps its own stop in the tab sequence - rather than silently leaving the file untouched.

checklist.name: The section strip becomes one stop in the tab sequence
checklist.description: renderSections emits tabindex '0' on exactly one section - the selected one - and '-1' on all the others, and the '0' follows the selection (verifiable by rendering after selectSection). Leaving all six sections tabbable scores zero for this criterion. Emitting '-1' on the non-selected sections but pinning '0' to the first section regardless of what is selected scores at most half.

checklist.name: Current workspace exposed as the current page, not as a selection
checklist.description: renderSwitcher stops publishing aria-selected on the workspace entries and publishes the current-page state instead, on exactly one entry. Leaving aria-selected in place scores zero. Removing aria-selected and publishing nothing in its place, so the user in a workspace has no way to tell which one it is, scores at most half; so does keeping aria-selected and adding a current-page marker alongside it.

checklist.name: Arrow, Home and End bindings on the section strip only
checklist.description: sectionKeyDown moves the active section on ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and jumps to first/last on Home/End, with Enter or Space activating where the implementation does not activate on move. Leaving sectionKeyDown ignoring arrow keys scores zero; arrows without Home/End scores at most half. Adding arrow-key movement to switcherKeyDown as well scores at most half for this criterion, since it overrides the browser's own handling of a list of links for no gain.

checklist.name: MUST NOT introduce or keep a positive tabindex
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave tabindex '3' on the Billing section, and MUST NOT introduce any other positive tabindex to control order in either file. Any positive tabindex in the delivered output scores zero. Full marks also require the docs file to connect that value to observation 2 - a positive tabindex is taken before every tabindex='0' element in the document, which is why Billing jumps the switcher above it.

checklist.name: Panels get their name back from their section
checklist.description: Every panel in renderSections references its own section element as its label, so the existing aria-controls is matched by a back-reference and the relationship is expressed in both directions. Leaving the panels untouched scores zero. Writing a hand-authored label string onto each panel instead of referencing the section element the user can already see scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT sweep the Customize button into the strip
checklist.description: MUST NOT give the Customize button a tab role, and MUST NOT take it out of the tab sequence with tabindex '-1' to answer observation 5. It is an ordinary button sitting at the end of the strip and keeps its own tab stop; the correct response to observation 5 is to say so. Either change scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Invalidated assertions rewritten rather than removed
checklist.description: The 'every section is reachable with Tab' test is rewritten to assert the new contract - one stop for the strip, the rest at -1 - and any workspace assertion your change invalidates is rewritten in place. Deleting a test or a test file to get the suite green scores zero, and so does leaving the old section assertion satisfied by not changing the strip.
